finding: The official contract requires nonfinite evaluation when an argument ball is not an analytic domain; it gives meromorphic callbacks as one sufficient example. The inspected transformed callbacks have only the possible singularity -2i/5. Although exponentiating z(t) can create an essential singularity there (so global meromorphic is inaccurate), each transformed expression evaluates lambda=i/[b(t+2i/5)] and propagates nonfinite evaluation on any ball containing this point. On every remaining ball the formulas compose rational functions with nonvanishing denominator and entire functions. No branch-cut operation occurs; the constant sqrt(3)/2 is computed outside the callback. This is a direct domain argument, rather than classification of the full integrands as meromorphic.
scope: API-domain check only; correct FLINT/Arb library implementation remains an external arithmetic dependency.
